semantic_rationale: The request explicitly leaves a material intent unresolved. Both supplied readings fit the fragment, so choosing one would invent user intent. Fixed operands elsewhere remain resolved.
semantic_review_notes: Replacing the explicit by Narela Umbrin clause with the note-dependent author condition changes a literal operand, so it cannot be accepted as meaning-preserving paraphrase. It is nevertheless justified under the supplied revision contract: the old clause supplies the very author value whose unresolved selection the calibration objective is intended to test. The replacement is confined to that conflicting author-selection mechanism, retains both names and the uncertain note, and preserves the title, every non-author filter and operating context. Keeping the old literal would preserve an already selected author and fail to cleanly instantiate this intended selection problem. The candidate remains in the intended AMBIGUOUS stratum; no author is invented or inferred.

The by-clause makes the author paired with the requested title a mandatory filter. Either supplied name could be associated with that title; the note gives no unique pairing and there is no external bibliographic evidence. An explicit title does not discharge the separately required selection from the note. Clarification is required. This is ambiguity of an existing required reference, rather than an absent task component, unsupported capability or contradiction.
